artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint against Korean Central Presbytery for administering a censure to a teaching elder before an indictment was drawn, in violation of BCO 32-3, and declared the underlying matter moot given that events occurred 21 years prior and the victim declined to participate. A concurring opinion argued the case should have been remanded to Presbytery for further action, and a dissenting opinion objected to declaring the case moot.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Neal Ganzel appealed his conviction and six-month suspension by Central Florida Presbytery for abuse of spiritual authority and related charges. The SJC unanimously sustained both specifications of error, finding that CFP violated BCO 32-20's one-year statute of limitations for most charges and committed numerous procedural missteps that rendered the disciplinary process significantly flawed and prejudicial, reversing the entire censure.

artifacts.synopsis: Ms. Doty and 21 others filed charges against a Nashville Presbytery teaching elder first with his congregation's Session (wrong court), then with Nashville Presbytery; Presbytery declined to indict and treated the matter as a report under BCO 31-2 rather than charges. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order (11-9-2-2) on the ground that Doty lacked standing under BCO 43-1 as a non-member of Nashville Presbytery; a significant dissent argued that her filing of charges gave her standing under prior precedent (Lyons, Ruff, Fordice).

artifacts.title: Bordwine v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE James Bordwine and others challenged Pacific Northwest Presbytery's handling of study reports on TE Peter Leithart's Federal Vision-related teachings and its refusal to declare those views either orthodox or out of accord with the Standards without judicial process. The SJC sustained the complaint, held that presbytery erred in declaring the views not out of accord, and remanded for pastoral counsel or BCO 31-2 action; concurring and dissenting opinions were recorded.
